div.head: Quadr II 8
div.ab: Et heæ quidem litteræ quanta regem decuit ueneratione susceptæ sunt, lectæ et perlectæ placuerunt; et quantus inde fructus sanctæ Dei ecclesiæ prouenerit, sequentia declarabunt.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 544 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Gerhard erhielt zwar das Pallium und für York das Metropolenrecht über Schottland (vgl. Raine Historians of York II 110), aber die königliche Gesandtschaft nicht Heinrichs wesentliche Forderung von Paschal zugestanden
Gerard did indeed receive the pallium and, for York, metropolitan rights over Scotland (cf. Raine Historians of York II 110), but the royal embassy was not granted Henry’s essential demand by Paschal
XVII Hk; Istae qu. Br, der das Folgende etwas verändert
XVII Hk; Istae qu. Br, who alters what follows somewhat
et fügt Macray [aus M?] zu Histor. mss. commission, twelfth report, app. IX p. 118
et added by Macray [from M?] Histor. mss. commission, twelfth report, app. IX p. 118
S. 544 vorl. Z. legere et perlegere wohl ‘lesen und wieder (nochmals) lesen’ wie persolvere im Wb
P. 544 penultimate l. legere et perlegere probably ‘to read and read again (once more)’, like persolvere in the Wb

div.ab: And these letters were received with as much veneration as befitted the king, and, read and read through, they gave pleasure; and how great a fruit came of it to the holy Church of God, what follows will declare.
